newsitem.title: USA: Former SEC lawyer pleads guilty in fraud case.
newsitem.headline: Former SEC lawyer pleads guilty in fraud case.

text.p: A former Securities and Exchange Commission lawyer pleaded guilty on Tuesday to defrauding the investors of companies he had been investigating.
James Nearen, a former attorney in the SEC's Denver office, pleaded guilty in Brooklyn federal court to three stock fraud counts and could face up to two years in prison and an $800,000 fine.
He is the last of six defendants to enter guilty pleas in the case.
Nearen pleaded guilty to buying discounted stock in Comprehensive Environmental Systems Inc and Alter Sales Corp and artifically inflating the price before selling it, prosecutors said.
Nearen went to work for Comprehensive in 1995, just weeks after the SEC fired him for revealing information about an investigation into the companies.
